resources.string: Farol only queries public information. It does not scan ports or try to access third-party systems. The requests made to the analyzed site are the same ones any browser would make.

To get the data, your searches are sent to external services: Google DNS sees the domains queried, Shodan InternetDB sees the IP addresses, and RDAP registries see the domain or IP whose ownership is looked up. With the My network option, the ipify service sees your public IP. The analyzed site also receives the connection request.

History and favorites are kept in memory on this device only and disappear when the app is closed; you can also delete them at any time. Your theme and timeout settings are saved on the device. The app has no server of its own, no accounts and no analytics. All requests use HTTPS.

A high score does not guarantee that a site is legitimate: a scam site can have a valid certificate. External databases may be out of date, and the absence of open ports or known vulnerabilities does not mean they do not exist. Use Farol as decision support, not as a verdict.
